author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Send the audit logs to the data collector with a TCP output in the json format on an appliance's LogForwarder function (TLS optional). The LogForwarder wraps each record as {"version":2,...,"hostname":<appliance>,"daemon":<daemon>,"log":{<record>}}, one per line. Records from rsyslog's [AUDIT] export (%msg:9:$% template) or the LogServer come unwrapped, with log_source as the appliance; the parser reads both, from the first brace, so a syslog header in front is fine. Sign-ins go to Auth: authentication_succeeded and _failed for clients and admins (authentication_type), password_ and otp_authentication for remedy actions, ssh_access to an appliance, and local_user_locked, with the user and identity provider from the distinguished name, the client address, the appliance, and the reason for a failure. ip_access goes to Netflow: the client's tunnel address to the endpoint, the protocol, allow or drop as the action, client to server for direction up, and the drop-reason as the end reason, with the user, client_ip, entitlement and rule in event_metadata. Administrator changes (entity_created, _updated and _deleted, settings updates, denylist entries, token and certificate revocations, remote commands, appliance actions) go to CloudAudit with the administrator, their address, the record type as the event name and the entity or user acted on as a resource. Every other record stays in generic. Appgate doesn't document the header of the TCP client's syslog format, and its ip_access example shows only allow; a drop is inferred from drop-reason. Samples are made up from the field tables and examples on Appgate's 6.7 Audit log detail and LogForwarder filtering pages. Entity records carry entity_type and event_type, as GitLab's audit events do; the library's GitLab audit events parser also asks for author_id and entity_path, which these records don't have, so it leaves them to this one. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (175 of 175 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (171 of 171 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). No built-in parser claimed these records. The entity_created sample, added later that day, passed the combined Run Test too (13 of 13 fields).
